name: Bilaan /blaan/
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand sources agree (1 agree, 0 refine), none contradicts
catalog_citation: Dean, James & Gladys Dean. 1955. The phonemes of Bilaan. Philippine Journal of Science 84(3): 311-322. Manila. [archive.org items pjs00317683vol84no3sep1955 and philippine-journal-of-science_1955-09_84_3, scanned text layers]
catalog_locator: p. 318, section 'STRESS', with its footnote (bottom of p. 318); fieldwork locale p. 313-314 (Sitio Kablan, foot of Mt. Matutum, Cotabato = Koronadal Blaan area)
catalog_quote: STRESS. A primary stress normally occurs on the ultima of a word base and a secondary stress on the antepenult of polysyllabic words.[fn] ... ayé gamilégu kifuh ani. 'that place to sleep mine night is' (That is my place to sleep tonight.) ... [fn:] When words are given in isolation, out of normal context, stress may vary. ... [p. 313-314:] The materials for this article were gathered over a period of approximately five months during the years of 1953-54 under the auspices of the Summer Institute of Linguistics. The main informant was a young man of twenty-one years, Arsenio Malayang Garciano, living in the Sitio of Kablan, near the foot of Mt. Matujum [Matutum].

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage, its footnote and the fieldwork locale are all present verbatim at the stated pages in the held Dean & Dean 1955 scanned (p. 318 STRESS section + footnote; p. 313 informant passage). (2) Deciding source is a primary 1955 SIL phonemic article by the fieldworkers -- the only 'phonology' item in Glottolog for any Blaan languoid; held Abrams 1970 (Koronadal morphology) is silent on stress. (3) downloaded now: Rhea 1995 CAD phonology summary -- 'Stress in Blaan is predictable; it occurs on the ultimate syllable of the root word' -- an independent fieldworker statement covering Blaan as a whole (author lived among Koronadal Blaan 1982-90), which confirms final (root-final) primary stress; it is silent on Dean's antepenult secondary stress.
